count.purpose: The live BB count; '/ target' on the same line at 0.5em in ink 3.

action.purpose: GO and STOP in the 96 px dock button.

wordmark.purpose: BULLOADER with an orange « + » on the connect screen.

state.purpose: The state word in its badge.

data.purpose: Battery, chips, fields: any measured or set number.

themes.mechanism: Each colour token is light-dark(light, dark); color-scheme follows the phone (Auto) unless data-theme='light'|'dark' pins it on <html>. Default Auto.

shadows.name: dialog-lift
shadows.purpose: The confirm dialog only; backdrop rgb(0 0 0 / 0.65).

shadows.name: banner-mask
shadows.purpose: Hides content scrolling under the sticky banner; not a visible shadow.

shadows.name: run-edge-glow
shadows.value: 0 0 0.5rem 0.125rem color-mix(in oklab, var(--tone) 70%, transparent), 0 0 1.25rem 0.25rem color-mix(in oklab, var(--tone) 35%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: Leading edge of the progress rule while running (orange) or slowing down (cyan). State only.

shadows.name: done-pulse
shadows.purpose: One pulse of the full bar on entering done (700 ms keyframe at 40%).

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Every control; fields use a 1 px accent-ink ring plus border instead.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The one easing for state changes.

motion.name: digit-tick
motion.purpose: A changed count digit drops into place. Transform only; short so it reads solid at 10+ BBs a second.

motion.name: state-change
motion.purpose: Colour and border transitions; the rule fill moves with scaleX in 160 ms linear.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce -> no animation, no transition

motion.name: haptics
motion.purpose: navigator.vibrate on the two endings worth feeling in a pocket.

breakpoints.name: column
breakpoints.value: 30rem max width, single column, 1rem gutters; no other breakpoints

extensions.scope: The app at /app/ only. The Starlight docs site does not use this world yet; planned.

narrative.overview:
The app is a measuring instrument, not a remote control. One number fills the screen: the count, in very large tabular mono, read from a metre away in the sun. Under the thumb sits one action, signal orange to start, solid ink to stop. Everything else is quiet: a graphite near-black ground in dark, a warm paper-white ground in light, hairline borders, tight corners, a faint drafting grid behind the header that fades out before the count.

The references are developer consoles like Neon and Supabase: flat panels, 1 px lines, mono for numbers and labels, one saturated accent. The world refuses the generic dark IoT remote with a stack of equal-weight cards. Hierarchy comes from size and position, not from boxes.

Both themes are first class. Auto (follow the phone) is the default; Réglages can pin Clair or Sombre. Every token has a light and a dark value, picked by the CSS `light-dark()` function, so a component is written once.
keyCharacteristics: One giant mono count with "/ target" at half size, and a thin progress rule with a tick every tenth.
One full-width 96 px action bar fixed at the bottom, in the thumb zone.
Signal orange is the only action colour; state colours are reserved and always come with a glyph and a word.
Hairline borders, 6-8 px corners, no decorative shadows.
Motion is short, transform-only and means something: digits tick, the leading edge glows while the motor runs, the bar pulses once on done.
Dark and light themes from one token set; Auto by default.

rules.name: The One Orange Rule
rules.body: Orange means "act" or "acting": GO, the primary button, the selected choice, the switch on, and the running state that GO started. Nothing decorative is orange except the « + » of the wordmark.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: Every state colour comes with its glyph and its word (badge, banner, field error, battery chip). A colour-blind player in sunlight reads the word.

rules.name: The Reserved State Rule
rules.body: Cyan is slowdown, green is done, magenta-red is jam or error, yellow is low battery or a warning. Do not borrow them for anything else.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Mono Rule
rules.body: Any number the device measures or the player sets is in Geist Mono with tabular figures, so digits never shift as they change.

rules.name: The Thumb Bar Rule
rules.body: The main action of a screen lives in the bottom dock, full width, 96 px tall. Only one main action is shown at a time: STOP while the motor turns, GO otherwise.

rules.name: The Glow Is State Rule
rules.body: Glow appears only to say what the machine is doing: the leading edge glows while the motor loads (running or slowdown) and the bar pulses once on done. Never as decoration, hover or emphasis.

dos: **Do** write every colour as one token with a light and a dark value (`light-dark()`), and test both themes plus Auto.
**Do** pair every state colour with its glyph and its word.
**Do** put the screen's one main action in the bottom dock, full width, 96 px.
**Do** keep every touch target at 56 px or more and every text at 4.5:1 on its ground.
**Do** set numbers in Geist Mono with tabular figures.
**Do** animate with transform and opacity only, keep it under 200 ms for anything that repeats, and honour reduced motion.
**Do** mark "off" with a dashed border and no fill, not with fading.
donts: **Don't** use orange for anything that is not an action, a selection, or the running state.
**Don't** use green for "fine" (a healthy battery is neutral); green means done.
**Don't** add glow or shadow for decoration; glow encodes state, the dialog is the only lifted surface.
**Don't** stack equal-weight cards; the count and the action dominate, the rest is one quiet panel.
**Don't** load fonts or anything else from the network; the app works offline.
**Don't** let a line appearing or a digit changing move the count.
